textbookText: 11. What are the group of magnesium and nitrogen? Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction between these two elements. Ans:- Magnesium belongs to Group 2, which is the alkaline earth metals, while nitrogen belongs to Group 15, also called the pnictogens. When magnesium is heated in the presence of nitrogen, it reacts to form magnesium nitride. The reaction can be represented by the balanced chemical equation: 3Mg + N₂ → Mg₃N₂ This is a combination reaction because two elements combine to form a single compound. 12. Rohan mixed 5 ml ammonium hydroxide and 5 ml hydrochloric acid in a test tube. i) What type of chemical reaction takes place in the test tube? Ans:- The reaction is a neutralization reaction because an acid reacts with a base to form a salt and water. ii) Write the balanced chemical equation of the above reaction. Ans:- The balanced chemical equation of the above reaction is NH₄OH + HCl → NH₄Cl + H₂O. iii) Write the name and nature of compound so formed. Ans:- The compound formed is ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl). It is a neutral salt. 12. Balance the following chemical reactions and mention their types.

a) KClO3 → KCl + O2 Ans:- Balanced chemical reaction is 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2 and it is Decomposition reaction (a single compound breaks down into simpler substances). b) CH4 + O2 → CO2 + H2O Ans:- Balanced chemical reaction is CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O and it is Combustion reaction (a hydrocarbon reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water). c) Fe + O2 → Fe2O3 Ans:- The balanced chemical reaction is 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3 and it is Combination reaction (two elements combine to form a single compound). d) Al + H2SO4 → Al2(SO4)3+ H Ans:- The balanced chemical reaction is 2Al + 3H2SO4 → Al2(SO4)3+ 3H2 and it is Displacement (single displacement) reaction (aluminum displaces hydrogen from sulphuric acid). 13. What is the rate of chemical reaction? Write any four factors which affect the rate of chemical reaction. Ans:- The rate of a chemical reaction is the speed at which reactants are converted into products. It is usually expressed as the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time. Four factors that affect the rate of chemical reaction are 1. Concentration of reactants: Higher concentration increases the rate because more particles are available for collisions. 2. Temperature: Increasing temperature increases the kinetic energy of particles, leading to more frequent and energetic collisions. 3. Surface area of reactants: A larger surface area allows more particles to collide at the same time, increasing the reaction rate. 4. Presence of a catalyst: A catalyst speeds up a reaction without being consumed by lowering the activation energy required.
